core_obligations: Set up the framework lemma: its assumptions (1) and (2) follow from the cited locality lemma for quasi-affine morphisms (proof lines 1898-1903).

Construct the descent datum \varphi : X' \times_Z Z' \to Z' \times_Z X' from representability and invoke effectivity of quasi-affine descent to get a quasi-affine Y \to Z with \psi : Z' \times_Z Y \to X' compatible with the descent data (proof lines 1905-1922).

Use the fpqc sheaf condition for X to obtain Y \to X from \psi \in \check{H}^0(\mathcal{Y}, X) and conclude via isomorphism descent that X is representable by a quasi-affine scheme (proof lines 1922-1937).
proof_roadmap: Feed the locality assumptions into the framework lemma.
Descend the datum effectively via the quasi-affine descent lemma.
Glue through the fpqc sheaf condition and descend the isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The proof is the quasi-affine twin of the affine descent argument: the framework lemma's assumptions come from the cited quasi-affine locality lemma; the descent datum \varphi is built from representability, effectivity of quasi-affine descent (cited) produces a quasi-affine Y \to Z, the fpqc sheaf condition turns \psi into Y \to X, and isomorphism descent concludes that X is representable by a quasi-affine scheme. The parallel structure with the affine case, with effectivity swapped to the quasi-affine lemma, is the substance.
